texto: In Dutch pain is expressed mainly in two ways: with «Ik heb pijn aan...» (I have pain in...: «Ik heb pijn aan mijn rug») or with the verb «pijn doen» (doll: «Mijn hoofd doet pijn», «Doet uw been ook pijn?»). «sinds» (from): «sinds gisteren» (from yesterday) is used to temporarily locate the start.

frases.nl: Ik heb pijn aan mijn rug.
Sinds gisteren. Mijn hoofd doet ook pijn.
frases.es: Desde ayer. También me duele la cabeza.
frases.en: Since yesterday. My head hurts, too.

frases.nl: Nee, alleen mijn rug en mijn hoofd.
frases.es: No, solo la espalda y la cabeza.
frases.en: No, just the back and the head.

bloques.pregunta: How is «My head hurts.» said in Dutch using the «pijn doen» verb?

opciones.explicacion: The verbal locution is «pijn doen», with the verb «doet» conjugated in singular.
It means «My head has a fever.», it's not the idiomatic expression.
«Kapot» applies to broken machines or objects, not parts of the human body.

bloques.pregunta: What symptom does the patient describe to the medical care provider?
bloques.frase: Ik heb pijn aan mijn rug.

opciones.texto: He's got a localized pain in his back.
opciones.explicacion: «Mijn rug» is the back and «pijn aan» expresses where it hurts.

opciones.texto: The right leg has been injured in the run.
opciones.explicacion: He doesn't mention the leg in this initial sentence.

opciones.texto: She's had a sore throat for a week.

bloques.pregunta: Complete the medical question about the patient's leg.

opciones.explicacion: Although it is an extremity, the assistant specifically asks for «uw been».
The patient had already declared the back pain before.

bloques.pregunta: When did the patient's discomfort begin?
bloques.frase: Sinds gisteren. Mijn hoofd doet ook pijn.

opciones.explicacion: «Sinds gisteren» sets the temporary start on the previous day.

opciones.texto: This very morning when I got up.

bloques.pregunta: Complete with the other part of the body that hurts the patient.
bloques.frase: Nee, alleen mijn rug en mijn ___.

opciones.explicacion: The patient has a pain in the back and head («mijn hoofd»).
The patient explicitly denies that his leg hurts.
It doesn't declare pain in the arm.

bloques.frase: Ik heb pijn aan mijn rug
bloques.explicacion: Fixed construction of body pain with «aan» preposition.
